claim: In default Kubernetes discovery mode, a pod is admitted to the routing pool only when its aggregate Ready condition (ContainersReady AND every condition in spec.readinessGates) is True; a False/Unknown Ready condition or a deletion timestamp removes it from the datastore. This K8s-specific admission gate has no automatic equivalent in file/custom discovery -- a custom plugin author must implement their own health gating before calling Upsert.
stance_target: a specific K8s-only safety mechanism (readiness gating) that a custom non-Kubernetes discovery backend must deliberately reimplement, since it does not come for free
scope_conditions: llm-d/llm-d-router, docs/discovery.md, 'Pod readiness in Kubernetes discovery' section, main branch, fetched Sep 11, 2026
quoted_support: In the default Kubernetes mode the EPP admits a pod into the routing pool only when the pod's aggregate Ready condition is True... A pod whose Ready condition is False or Unknown, or that has a deletion timestamp, is removed from the datastore and receives no traffic.

scope_conditions: llm-d/llm-d-router, docs/discovery.md, 'Overview' section, main branch, fetched Sep 11, 2026
quoted_support: The EPP does not call ctrl.GetConfig() or start a controller manager. The EPP does not require an InferencePool CRD or any K8s RBAC. The runner emits a one-time startup log naming these.
stance_target: file-discovery-mode llm-d deployments have full feature parity with Kubernetes deployments

quoted_support: InferenceModelRewrite (model name rewriting for traffic split or canary). The reconciler is not started; ds.ModelRewriteGet returns nil for every request. There is no file-mode equivalent today.

claim: The --pool-namespace value is resolved in order: (1) the --pool-namespace CLI flag, (2) the NAMESPACE environment variable (populated automatically by Kubernetes' Downward API), (3) the literal fallback string 'default'; outside Kubernetes neither of the first two is normally set, so operators should pass --pool-namespace explicitly or the pool is labeled with the Kubernetes-flavored but meaningless string 'default'. The runner emits a startup warning when it falls back.
stance_target: concrete operational guidance for correctly labeling metrics/logs in a non-Kubernetes deployment
scope_conditions: llm-d/llm-d-router, docs/discovery.md, 'Pool namespace' section, main branch, fetched Sep 11, 2026
quoted_support: On bare metal, in Slurm, in Ray, or in any container without the Downward API, neither source is set and the pool is labeled default - a Kubernetes-flavored string that is meaningless outside K8s. Pass --pool-namespace explicitly so labels reflect your environment.

claim: In file discovery mode, --pool-name is optional and defaults to 'epp' if unset; its value is arbitrary and does not need to correspond to any Kubernetes object.
stance_target: the router's CLI/config surface is genuinely decoupled from Kubernetes naming concepts in file-discovery mode, not merely tolerant of their absence
scope_conditions: llm-d/llm-d-router, docs/discovery.md, 'Running EPP with file discovery' section, main branch, fetched Sep 11, 2026
quoted_support: --pool-name is optional in file discovery mode and defaults to epp if unset. It is used as the internal pool identifier in the scheduler and metrics. The value is arbitrary - it does not need to match any Kubernetes object.
